feedback.problem: Let $A$ be the set of all multiples of $2$ greater than $0$ and  let $B$ be the set of all multiples of $4$ greater than $0.$  What is $A∖B?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The multiples of $2$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
A={2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,…}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
B={4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32,36,…}.
$$

Now, $A∖B$ is the *difference* of $A$ and $B,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $A$ but *not* in $B.$

The elements of $A$ that are also in $B$ are $4,8,12,16,$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $4$). So, we must remove these elements from $A.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A∖B & ={2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,…}-{4,8,12,16,…} \\  & ={2,6,10,14,…}.\end{aligned}
$$
